facts.title: Fuji framed by a claw of water
facts.body: Hokusai’s Great Wave (c. 1831), from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, uses Prussian blue to make a cresting wave tower over boats — and over sacred Fuji itself.

facts.title: A wall of water
facts.body: The wave fills the left and center like a living mountain, dwarfing everything human beneath it.

facts.title: Fuji as a small white cone
facts.body: Mount Fuji sits low and quiet in the hollow of the wave — sacred and almost overlooked until you find it.

facts.title: Foam becoming talons
facts.body: The breaking edge turns into claw-like droplets — nature given a predator’s silhouette.

facts.title: Boats under the crest
facts.body: Three fast cargo boats (oshiokuri-bune) slide through the trough, tiny against the water’s architecture.

facts.title: Bodies braced for the smash
facts.body: Rowers huddle low, clinging to the moment before the wave’s weight arrives.

facts.title: A emptied sky
facts.body: The upper right sky is almost blank — calm against the print’s violent foreground.

facts.title: Imported blue, Japanese sea
facts.body: Hokusai’s deep Prussian blue was a newly popular imported pigment — modernity dyed into an iconic Japan.
